sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Smart Utility Meters and Remote Telemetry Sensors

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with strong administrative law influence and commercial law codification in the Code de commerce)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between France and the United States for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion (1994, as amended)
Agreement between France and the People's Republic of China on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (2007 revision)
Agreement between France and Singapore for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (1977, as amended)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the EU (provisionally applied)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L561-1 through L561-60-2 and R561-1 et seq., transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; UBO register filing obligation under Article L561-46 and Article L561-2-2; implementing Decree No. 2016-1456 of 28 October 2016; INPI manages the UBO register for the Registre National des Entreprises. Additional AML/CFT obligations are set by the National Financial Intelligence Unit (Tracfin) instructions and ACPR (Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution) guidelines.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of legal existence (or equivalent extract from the foreign trade/company registry) of every non-French corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; where the origin jurisdiction is not a Hague Convention member, full Consular Legalization through the French Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney executed by all foreign shareholders and managers authorizing the French incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each beneficial owner's passport or national identity document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent administrative authority in the beneficial owner's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or recent bank statement for each beneficial owner and corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution licensed in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, shareholders, managers and commercial counterparties against the UN Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, French national asset freezes issued by the Direction générale du Trésor, and OFAC SDN list where a US nexus exists. PEP determination is mandatory for all UBOs and managers in accordance with FATF recommendations and CMF Article R561-20-3; enhanced due diligence is required where the client or a close associate/family member is a PEP. Ongoing transaction monitoring is structured around Tracfin mandatory reports and the French AML/CFT risk-based approach.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI – Registre National des Entreprises via the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; availability verification performed through the INPI data platform (data.inpi.fr) and the RCS database available via Infogreffe.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French company names may contain French or foreign language words but must be expressed in Latin script. Everything filed in the name and corporate documents must be transliterated into Latin characters; if the foreign language uses non-Latin script, an official French translation or standardized transliteration is required. The name must be lawful, distinctive, not misleading, and must include the legal form 'SARL' or 'société à responsabilité limitée' for the SARL vehicle.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a formal administrative name reservation; however, the pre-clearance report and initial availability check are treated as valid for 30 days for incorporation planning purposes. If the INPI/Greffe rejects the proposed name, the applicant or its counsel may file a written reconsideration request with the Registre National des Entreprises within 15 days of notification, invoking Articles L. 711-1 to L. 711-4 of the Intellectual Property Code and Article L. 123-9 of the Commercial Code; if rejected a second time, an administrative appeal may be brought before the administrative court of the registered office location, or the applicant may elect to modify the name and resubmit through the Guichet Unique.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual office is not acceptable for ISIC 2651 manufacture of smart electricity meters. French law (Law No. 84-148 and Articles L123-11-1 et seq. of the Commercial Code) permits administrative domiciliation with an approved domiciliation company, but industrial manufacturing requires a declared physical establishment, equipment, premises and local personnel. A domiciliation agreement can support the registered office for legal correspondence, but the operational production site must be identified and properly covered by permits, safety inspections and social declarations. A virtual office without actual industrial substance will expose the company to regulatory penalties, tax recharacterization, and inability to obtain the required manufacturing license under the Code de l'énergie and electrical equipment conformity regulations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 60% risk of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 12 months of operation due to equipment safety, CE-marking conformity, electrical installation compliance, and labour/environmental controls; increasing to approximately 70% over a three-year horizon given customs and market surveillance authorities' focus on smart meters and IoT telemetry transmitting devices.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting, review and legalization instruction of the French SAS/SARL articles of association (statutes), including UBO declaration preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French avocat (business law firm) retained by the founders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; capped fixed-fee engagement in accordance with AZAvocat / Paris Bar customary fee schedules.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name pre-clearance and trademark/company-name availability search against INPI and RCS databases, including a preliminary IP conflict report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per professional search and written clearance opinion.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of the incorporation dossier with the INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut national de la propriété industrielle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government e-filing fee, statutory fixed tariff published in the Arrêté of 2 December 2021.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the SARL with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS entry and issuance of Kbis extract)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule (tarif des greffiers) set by the Ministry of Justice; current applicable tariff index.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the mandatory legal announcement (annonce légale) in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: JAL authorized by the prefecture of the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory maximum tariff for a 10-15 line company formation announcement; varies by department.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Domiciliation agreement with a licensed commercial domiciliation provider (first 12 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) approved by the relevant prefecture
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark in Paris / Hauts-de-France; average monthly fee converted to USD.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign corporate and personal documents (6-document bundle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of each foreign jurisdiction plus French Embassy/Consulate where required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory/per-document tariff in the origin country and standard consular legalization fee of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of foreign corporate documents, apostilled documents, powers of attorney and supporting UBO evidence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) registered with a French cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per source page; average of 25 pages at statutory/court-approved translation rates.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-56 (SARL); Articles L.123-1 et seq. (RCS registration); Decree No. 2023-200 of 20 March 2023 (Guichet unique formalities); relevant provisions of the Monetary and Financial Code for capital deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, with electronic filing through the INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de constitution d'une société (company formation application), comprising signed statutes and all annexes submitted to the RCS through the INPI Guichet unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SARL. The capital is fixed freely in the articles and must be fully subscribed. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked French bank account or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; funds are released only after registration and issuance of the K-bis. At least one fifth of each cash contribution must be paid up before filing unless the statutes require full payment; the remainder must be paid within five years. In-kind contributions must be fully paid up at formation and, if required, accompanied by a contribution auditor's report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY BY THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF THE COMPANY ON [DATE]. Whereas the formation documents have been reviewed, it is resolved: (1) The share capital of EUR [•] is declared fully and irrevocably subscribed and allotted as stated in the Articles of Association, and the deposit of cash funds in a blocked French bank account, evidenced by the attestation de dépôt de fonds, is approved. (2) The registered office is fixed at [address], within the territorial jurisdiction of the RCS of [city], and is adopted. (3) [Full name] is appointed as Manager (Gérant) for an indefinite term, with full powers to bind the company within its corporate purpose. (4) The Articles of Association and this resolution are ratified, and the Manager is authorised to complete and file all registration formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal drafting and execution of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders, corporate counsel or notaire in France
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SARL statutes in French under Articles L.223-1 et seq. of the Commercial Code. Include exact corporate name, legal form, registered office, corporate purpose covering smart utility meter manufacturing and IoT connectivity, share capital, share allocation, and manager powers. Verify the manager's eligibility and obtain a non-bankruptcy declaration and documents supporting the registered office. Sign the statutes in original or by means of a notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Draft statutes prepared in French
Signed statutes or notarial act
Identity document of each founding shareholder
Criminal record or police certificate of the proposed manager as required
Supporting document for registered office (lease or ownership title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a substantive legal deficiency is identified by counsel, the registrar, or the notaire, amend the relevant article, re-execute the statutes, and reperform any capital deposit verification before filing. No capital funds may be withdrawn until registration is complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of subscribed share capital in blocked account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a company-in-formation bank account in the name of the future SARL. Deposit the required paid-in portion of each cash contribution, at least one fifth unless full payment is required by the articles. Obtain the bank's attestation de dépôt de fonds, which must be included in the later filing. Notify the bank that the funds are blocked in favour of the company until production of the K-bis registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Attestation de dépôt de fonds issued by the bank
Draft statutes or formation extract containing company details and capital
Bank account mandate and opening forms
Identity documents of persons signing the deposit instruction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the company-in-formation account or the deposit, engage a notaire to hold the capital in escrow, or deposit with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations. An alternative certificate from the escrow holder is equally accepted by the Guichet unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorised in the department of the registered office, selected via the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the formal notice containing the company name, legal form, capital amount, registered office, corporate purpose, manager name, and the RCS court where registration will occur. Pay the gazette fee and cause publication in an authorised legal gazette. The publication proof is automatically or manually attached to the formation dossier.
required_dossiers: Text of the legal announcement (avis de constitution)
Declaration confirming the authorised JAL chosen
Certificate of publication issued by the JAL
Payment receipt for announcement fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal gazette identifies errors or omissions, correct the announcement and republish immediately. Where republication is required, adjust the filing sequence in the Guichet unique; the registry will compute the effective publicity date from the valid publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of formation dossier with Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI — Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online formation questionnaire, select the SARL form, and upload all statutory documents. The electronic dossier routes the registration to the RCS/Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and, where relevant, to tax and social administrations. Ensure all scanned signatures are compliant and that the legal announcement deposit certificate is included. Confirm receipt of the systematic acknowledgement with a dossier number.
required_dossiers: Signed statutes
Bank capital deposit attestation
Certificate of legal announcement publication
Registered office proof (lease, ownership, or consent)
Identity documents of founders and manager
Manager's non-bankruptcy declaration
Beneficial owner declaration, if filed at this point
Payment receipts for all mandatory ancillary fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet unique rejects or queries the dossier, access the same electronic folder and cure within fifteen days of the notification. Add or correct the requested pages, revalidate, and resubmit without paying a fresh official state filing fee. Failure to cure may require a new filing with a new date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of K-bis certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce — Registre du commerce et des sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following administrative validation, the Greffe registers the company on the RCS and issues the extrait K-bis, the official proof of legal existence and commercial capacity. The registration triggers the release of the blocked capital funds, which the bank or Caisse des Dépôts may remit to the company upon presentation of the K-bis. Verify that the registered corporate purpose exactly reflects the smart meter manufacturing and IoT telemetry activity.
required_dossiers: No additional document unless the Greffe requests a clarification
K-bis request or generated registration extract
Final valid dossier from the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues an observation, correct the specific inconsistency via the Guichet unique within fifteen days. Should the registration be refused, appeal the refusal before the premier président de la cour d'appel within the applicable time limit or resubmit a remediated dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial owner declaration and social registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI / RCS (for UBO), INSEE and URSSAF social registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial owner declaration with the RCS within thirty days of registration. Ensure that the company receives its SIREN, SIRET, and VAT intra-community number. Register the gérant and employees, if any, with URSSAF and issue a RIB for tax and social payments.
required_dossiers: UBO declaration form filed electronically
K-bis extract
Identity documents and proof of address of each beneficial owner
Statutes and deed of appointment of manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UBO declaration is deficient, submit a corrective declaration through the Guichet unique and notify the Greffe. False or incomplete declarations can be cured before enforcement procedures; voluntarily corrected filings may reduce or eliminate penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of tax, VAT, and EORI registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP); Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects for EORI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transfer the K-bis, articles, and resolution to the corporate tax office; select the corporate income tax regime applicable to SARL; obtain the French VAT number; and, if goods will be imported from non-EU suppliers, request an EORI number. Keep this certificate in the compliance file for customs clearance and for opening bank accounts operated by payment-rail counterparties.
required_dossiers: K-bis extract
Articles of association
First board resolution or deed appointing the manager
Bank account details
EORI application form if import or export operations are planned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGFIP does not issue the VAT number after two weeks, follow up through the local tax office by submitting the filing receipt and confirm the commencement date. For late registration, request a rescript or request an extension via the Conciliateur Fiscal; any automatic late-filing penalty can be abated if the underlying facts are promptly and voluntarily regularised.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE), Ministère de l'Économie et des Finances; conformity assessment body such as LNE (Laboratoire National de Métrologie et d'Essais) for metrological approval of measuring instruments.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Attestation d'examen CE de type / Certificat d'assurance qualité de production under Directive 2014/32/EU (Measuring Instruments Directive, Annex MI-003) for active electrical energy meters, together with CE marking declaration of conformity and, where applicable, French metrological authorisation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires — DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Light notification for low-impact electronic assembly of smart meters; full EIA (étude d'impact) required only where the facility triggers ICPE authorisation due to surface treatment, solvent use, waste treatment thresholds, or feedstock processing. If registration or authorisation thresholds are met, an ICPE self-monitoring and environmental analysis regime applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater must meet municipal sewer pre-treatment limits and the general water law requirements under Articles L.210-1 et seq. of the Environmental Code; VOC emissions from soldering and coating operations must comply with Directive 2010/75/EU and the French arrêté of 2 February 1998 if solvent consumption exceeds thresholds. Hazardous electronic waste, batteries, and solder residues must be tracked by bordereau de suivi de déchets dangereux and treated through REACH-registered channels in accordance with EU Battery Directive 2006/66/EC and WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety verification by the service départemental d'incendie et de secours for any open-to-public or large workplace area; structural load and electrical compliance attestation issued by an approved inspection body such as APAVE or Bureau Veritas; occupational risk assessment and DUERP (Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels) must be maintained; operator workplace clearance confirmed through URSSAF registration and payment of branch-specific social contributions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – registration through the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); direct VAT/PE registration at the territorial SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises); digital portal impots.gouv.fr; customs EORI allocation by Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) via DELTA-X
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly incorporated SARL is registered by operation of law through the Guichet Unique, which automatically delivers the SIREN/SIRET and the intra-Community VAT number (format FR + 11 alphanumeric digits, i.e., FR + 2-digit key + 9-digit SIREN) within approximately one week of incorporation; no separate VAT application is required for the domestic French establishment. For export operations, the SARL must additionally obtain an EORI number (FR + SIREN) from the DGDDI customs system DELTA-X. A non-established foreign entity engaging in French taxable transactions (e.g., a foreign parent selling IoT hardware in France) must apply directly to the SIE using Form 1442-SD, attach certified proof of incorporation, the list of directors, residency certificates of officers, and a signed power of attorney; if the entity is established outside the EU, appointment of a fiscally responsible representative (représentant fiscal) is compulsory under Article 289 A CGI. A foreign entity with a French permanent establishment must file Form 1477-SD with the SIE and, where it is the EU-registered operator, present its EORI and appoint a customs representative for export clearance. The SARL itself, being French, requires no parent-company tax approval; non-resident shareholders merely supply a tax residency certificate for treaty benefit claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SARLs are default-taxed under French corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés – IS) at 25% (reduced 15% rate for SMEs with turnover ≤ €10 million, share capital fully paid, and ≥75% individually-owned capital – Art. 219-I-b CGI). Available elective regimes: (1) Option for pass-through/partnership taxation (Impôt sur le Revenu – IR) under Article 239 bis AA CGI for family SARLs or SARLs less than five years old, meeting the statutory shareholder/activity conditions, irrevocable for five years; (2) Fiscal integration (intégration fiscale, Article 223 A CGI) for a French parent holding at least 95% of the SARL's shares, permitting full group consolidation of tax results; (3) Election to apply the participation exemption (régime mère-fille, Article 145 CGI) for qualifying French/EU/non-EU shareholdings of at least 5% held for two years, providing 95% exemption from corporate tax; (4) Anti-hybrid and notional-interest elections under Article 212 bis and BOI-INT-DIF-360-20 for cross-border financing and hybrid mismatch avoidance; (5) The statutory option for the franchise en base de TVA (VAT small-business exemption) for annual turnover under €85,000, which is a genuine election disapplying normal VAT rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (French Value Added Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic: no minimum threshold – any French business making taxable supplies of goods or services must be registered for TVA, and the SARL holds its VAT number automatically from incorporation. Franchise en base de TVA (optional small-business exemption): €85,000 annual turnover for all activities from 1 January 2025 (implementing the EU SME Directive 2020/285; replacing the former differentiated thresholds of €91,900 for goods and €36,800 for services); this exemption covers only pure domestic supplies and denies input VAT recovery. Intra-EU distance sales to French consumers: €10,000 EU-wide aggregation threshold, after which OSS registration or local French VAT registration is required. Non-established foreign suppliers that place IoT equipment or provide remote telemetry services in France have no exemption threshold and must register directly for TVA from the first taxable transaction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France operates a mandatory B2B e-invoicing and e-reporting regime for all VAT-liable persons established in France: large enterprises (grandes entreprises) and mid-size enterprises (ETI) must issue structured e-invoices from 1 September 2026; SMEs (including this SARL if it qualifies as an SME) must comply from 1 September 2027; all taxable persons must be able to receive e-invoices from 1 September 2026. The regime is a 3-corner Y-model without digital stamping: invoices are routed through the public platform PPF (Portail Public de Facturation) or a certified partner dematerialisation platform (PDS), exchanging the required data fields in Factur-X, UBL 2.1, or CII (D16B) formats via secure APIs (machine-to-machine). E-reporting (transmission to DGFiP of summary data for cross-border B2B supplies and B2C transactions) is mandatory from the same dates. Non-compliance with e-invoicing obligations triggers penalties under Article 1737 CGI (€15 per missing or non-compliant invoice, capped at €150,000 per calendar year, with reduced caps for SMEs) and obstruction of tax audit may lead to summary assessment under Articles 1730–1732 CGI.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% TVA rate applies to: (a) definitive exports of smart electricity meters and related IoT hardware physically leaving the EU customs territory (Article 262-I-1° CGI), evidenced by a customs export declaration (H1/DAE accepted in DELTA-X with a Movement Reference Number), physical transport of goods, and exit confirmation recorded by the customs office of export within 90 days of acceptance, extendable to 150 days (Articles 329 and 333-0 CGI, Annex III); (b) intra-EU dispatches of manufactured meters to a VAT-registered customer in another Member State at 0% under Article 262-ter CGI, requiring the customer's valid EU VAT number, issuance of the invoice, and monthly filing of the ECSL/DEB declaration; and (c) technically connected offshore services – installation, calibration, firmware provisioning, and remote telemetry data services supplied to non-EU clients – which are outside French VAT territoriality under Articles 259, 259-A to 259-C CGI where the effective use and enjoyment occurs outside the EU. For all categories, the exporter must demonstrate the commercial reality of the flow (contract, Incoterms, transport instructions, payment trace); failure to substantiate the chain reclassifies the supply as taxable at 20% TVA.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAE/H1 in DELTA-X) with MRN and customs exit confirmation
Bill of Lading (original or electronic negotiable copy with discharge stamps) / CMR / IATA Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificat de change or bank Swift MT103) evidencing FX repatriation of the export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and French Customs (DGDDI) jointly audit export zero-rating claims; all export proof must be retained for 6 years (Article L102 B of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales) and produced within 30 days of an audit request. Where the 90/150-day evidence window is missed, the supply is reassessed at 20% TVA plus late interest (intérêts de retard at 0.20% per calendar month); in bad-faith cases a 40% penalty applies (Article 1729 CGI), escalating to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres, plus a €750 fine per documentary irregularity (Article 1788 A CGI). Although the general exchange-control repatriation obligation for goods export proceeds was liberalised, the 180-day benchmark remains the reference standard for export commercial terms and for documentary acceptance; payment terms exceeding 180 days require documented justification in the audit file. Criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI (false invoicing, round-tripping, fabricated customs certificates) is available, carrying up to €500,000 fine and 5 years' imprisonment for the responsible legal representatives. In a fraudulent chain, the State may declare the French exporting SARL jointly liable under Article 1691 bis CGI for the unpaid VAT of its non-established supplier or customer, and the exporter loses entitlement to the reduced corporate tax rate and innovation-related credits, with input VAT clawed back and secured by a customs guarantee (sûreté) for continuing zero-rated exports.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) — central bank vested with balance-of-payments statistics and cross-border transaction reporting under Article L141-6 of the Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF); foreign-exchange and capital-movement policy administered jointly by the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; prudential supervision exercised by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for credit institutions and payment/EMI institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account operations; France applies the EU free-movement-of-capital principle (Art. 63 TFEU, Articles L151-1 and L151-2 CMF). No exchange-control authorization is required for profit remittance, dividends, loan repayments, royalties, or trade settlement. Residual barriers: (i) prior FDI screening authorization under Article L151-3 CMF for non-EU/EEA direct investments in sensitive sectors, extended by Decree 2019-1590 and the 31 December 2023 decree to activities affecting the integrity, security, or continuity of energy infrastructure — smart-grid metering equipment that interoperates with public distribution networks and supplies critical data to grid operators may be captured, requiring a legal perimeter memo; (ii) statutory balance-of-payments (BOP) reporting to the Banque de France for all flows, and specific reporting of direct investments above €1,000,000; (iii) dividend distributions to non-EU parents are unrestricted but may be subject to withholding tax (0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for eligible EU/EEA shareholders; 5–15% under DTTs such as FR–US, FR–CN). The capital account is open with only declarative and screening constraints, not quantitative exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds exists in France; the exchange-control regime was liberalized in 1990 (Law 89-1008). Exporters may retain receivables in any currency and are not required to convert into EUR within any statutory window. Obligations are limited to: (i) BOP reporting of every individual non-resident transaction equal to or exceeding €12,500 (aggregated weekly per counterparty where applicable) — typically discharged monthly by the intermediary bank in the 'filière déléguée' unless the company opts for direct reporting to the Banque de France; (ii) arm's-length pricing of export receivables under Article 57 CGI — receivables systematically outstanding beyond 12 months may be challenged as deemed distributions or transfer-pricing adjustments; (iii) statutory accounts must be kept in EUR, with unrealized FX differences booked per the French PCG or IFRS; (iv) export invoices for IoT hardware should specify a market-standard payment term (60–180 days) and be settled via SWIFT MT103 with a BOP category evidencing merchandise trade (goods sold), so the receivables remain traceable and hedgeable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte séquestre / dépôt des fonds) and Operational Account (compte courant)
Operational Account (compte courant professionnel) with trade finance and LC facility
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE / Natixis (Groupe BPCE, Banque Populaire branches)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (via Banque Populaire regional desks)
Operational Account with export factoring line
Operational Account (basic payment services and universal banking access)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-High for operational treasury, Low for capital escrow. ACPR-licensed or EU-passported EMIs (Qonto, Shine, Wise Europe, Revolut Bank UAB under EU passporting into France) provide rapid remote onboarding, SEPA and SWIFT settlement, multi-currency IBANs (EUR, USD, GBP), and strong API integration for trade flows of a smart-meter manufacturer. Legal constraints: (i) EMIs cannot hold the SARL's initial share capital as a blocked escrow account because the certificat de dépôt des fonds required by Article L223-7 of the French Commercial Code for Greffe registration must be issued by a credit institution or a notary — a pure EMI certificate is not accepted by the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés; (ii) EMIs cannot provide overdrafts, documentary credits (LC), or trade-loan facilities; (iii) safeguarded client funds of pure EMIs are not covered by the Fonds de Garantie des Dépôts et de Résolution (FGDR) unless the entity holds a full banking licence (e.g., Revolut Bank UAB passported), although segregation requirements mitigate; (iv) some EMIs impose stricter sectoral filters on 'manufacturing' or dual-use-adjacent technology — a smart-meter IoT business must be prepared to supply EORI, HS-6 classification (9028.30 for electricity meters, 9030 for telemetry), and end-user attestations. Recommended architecture: EMI for day-to-day collections/disbursements and multi-currency balances, with a Tier-1 bank as the anchor for capital escrow, LC issuance, and FX/derivative lines. If the Tier-1 bank refuses an account on risk grounds, the company may exercise the right to a basic account under Article L312-1 CMF by requesting the Banque de France to designate an institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permitted: French AML regulation (Articles L561-5-1 and R561-5 CMF, implementing the EU AML Directives) allows electronic identity verification via eIDAS-certified means, video-verification with ACPR-approved providers (e.g., France Identité, VERIFI), and cross-border e-ID recognition. Fully remote onboarding is the norm for a SARL with resident EU managers holding a passport or e-ID. However, bank internal risk policies frequently impose one physical interview with the gérant (or a legal representative) where: (i) the beneficial owner is located outside the EU/EEA; (ii) the business targets critical energy infrastructure; or (iii) the mandate includes LC issuance or hybrid treasury limits. For the capital escrow account, the bank requires the notarized statuts, the founders' declaration, and the formal request to the Greffe — these can be delivered digitally via the Guichet Unique, but non-resident shareholders' signatures may require apostille/legalization (Hague Convention) and a certified French translation. There is no statutory physical-presence mandate; the decisive factor is the bank's risk appetite. Mitigant for a fully remote outcome: appoint a French-based cabinet d'expertise comptable as authorized interlocutor under a power of attorney and open through the bank's international desk (e.g., BNP Paribas Business International, Société Générale Internationale).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or intervening parent resident in a jurisdiction on the EU/FATF high-risk or grey list (e.g., overseas tax-havens or non-supervised centres) causing automatic enhanced due diligence and possible refusal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full BO organigram per 5AMLD covering every 25%+ ownership layer; tax residence certificates; FATF- or EU-style country risk assessment memo; bank reference letter from a regulated home-country bank; evidence of economic substance (headcount, premises, payroll) in the intermediate jurisdiction; regulator-approved group AML policy; commitment to monthly transaction reporting and sub-account transparency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of wealth or unsubstantiated funding of the SARL initial share capital or subsequent capital injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements or a sworn expert-comptable attestation of the contributing entity covering the last three fiscal years; parent board resolution approving the capital contribution; notarized subscription certificate; traceable payment trail (SWIFT MT103 from the remitting bank); signed source-of-wealth declaration with supporting liquidation or retained-earnings proof; tax clearance certificate from the contributor's tax authority; negative no-liens search.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP (politically exposed person) status of the gérant, manager, or 25%+ shareholder (foreign or domestic) triggering enhanced scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP declaration per ACPR practice; detailed CV and professional references; employment contract or commercial registration of the PEP's employer; news-search / negative-media report with a clean certified result; justification of the source of funds for the contribution; confirmation that the PEP is not subject to UN/EU/OFAC sanctions; consent to periodic enhanced review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-sector and end-user risk: smart electricity meters and IoT telemetry devices are adjacent to critical-energy infrastructure and cybersecurity, raising dual-use or sanctions-diversion concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU Dual-Use Regulation (EU) 2021/821 classification memo demonstrating exclusion (standard utility meter without high-grade encryption or grid-control functions) or, if applicable, valid export authorization; ISO 27001 / IEC 62443 certificates; end-user attestations for all foreign clients; UN/EU/OFAC sanctions screening logs (World-Check or equivalent); restricted-party screening policy; corporate trade-compliance manual; EORI number and HS-6 classification 9028.30 / 9030 / 8537 with completed deny-party and consolidated-screening checks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate documentation gaps or ownership opacities — incomplete Kbis, unfiled beneficial-ownership declaration at the Guichet Unique, nominee arrangements, or invalid representation of foreign shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original Kbis extract issued less than 3 months before onboarding; notarized and where necessary apostilled statuts of the SARL with certified French translation; proof of registered office (bail commercial or ownership deed); confirmation of the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs declaration; constitutional documents of each shareholder in the chain (certified copies); shareholders' register; written confirmation that no nominee or trust holds interests; valid power of attorney for any representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to evidence the commercial purpose of cross-border payments (e.g., inbound equity contribution versus service fee) causing floating or mis-coded BOP declarations to the Banque de France and potential fines under L165-1 CMF.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction purpose code memorandum for the remitting and receiving banks; signed investment agreement or capital-increase resolution; pro-forma invoices and master contracts for trade; copy of the BOP declaration acknowledgement (direct filing or filière déléguée); standardized SWIFT Field 70 text ('APPORT_EN_CAPITAL_SOCIAL' for equity, 'TRADE_GOODS' for merchandise); reconciliation of the bank ledger to the company's cash-flow statement; monthly BOP cutoff certificates from the expert-comptable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for share-capital injection from a non-resident parent: (1) FDI screening — if the parent is non-EU/EEA and the smart-meter activity touches the energy-infrastructure perimeter of Article L151-3 CMF (e.g., grid-network interoperability, cybersecurity functionality of the meter's telemetry module, or long-term supply to distribution system operators), file a prior authorization request with the DG Trésor before settlement; if outside the perimeter, retain a legal memo confirming exemption; (2) settlement via SWIFT MT103 from the parent's bank to the French receiving bank (BNP Paribas or Société Générale) with Field 70 citing 'APPORT_EN_CAPITAL_SOCIAL_2025_AUGMENTATION_DE_CAPITAL' and the BOP category for equity capital; include the parent's resolution and the subscription list for the bank's KYC file; (3) for an existing SARL, the funds must be deposited in a bank-blocked 'compte séquestre' until the gérant signs the declaration of subscription and payment and the Greffe updates the Kbis; alternatively a notary or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations may act as depositary; (4) report the direct investment to the Banque de France within 20 days following the month-end if the transaction value exceeds €1,000,000 (Form 'Investissements directs' via the bank's filière or direct filing); every flow above €12,500 is captured in the monthly BOP declaration; (5) verify origin of funds — the remitting bank must provide a correspondent reference and, where the amount is disproportionate to the parent's equity, the beneficiary bank will request audited accounts or a certified treasury statement; (6) FX conversion, if the parent remits USD or CNY, is a spot transaction against the ECB reference rate plus margin and is unrestricted; (7) after receipt, update the RCS and the share register through the Guichet Unique, and where capital introduces in-kind contributions (e.g., patents, prototypes), obtain a commissaire aux apports valuation before the notarial deed is completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operational procurement and project-milestone payments: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments in EUR/USD/CNY with Field 70 purpose-code referencing (merchandise purchases, components, or services) — 48–72-hour processing on the SWIFT network; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and Instant SCT for EU-based suppliers and subcontractors settling in EUR (0–10 seconds for instant, ideal for urgent sub-assembly orders); (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 issued by the French anchor bank in favor of suppliers for raw-material or sub-assembly purchases, commonly confirmed by a bank in the supplier's jurisdiction — for milestone-based smart-meter projects, use a revolving LC in tranches triggered by warehouse inspection reports, packing lists, and EN 50470 / MID 2014/32/EU metrology certificates; (iv) Documentary collections under URC 522 for low-risk repeat shipments with bill of lading as the controlling document; (v) Escrowed milestone payments — use an escrow agent bank instruction letter for IoT deployment projects (e.g., 30% prepayment, 40% at DAP incoterms delivery, 20% at commissioning, 10% at the end of the 12-month performance guarantee); (vi) For export sales to French grid operators or international utilities, the SARL may act as beneficiary under an export LC, and the French bank's forfaiting desk can discount the LC proceeds to shorten receivables days; (vii) All outward wires require UN/EU/OFAC screening of the beneficiary and verification of the high-risk item list — the company should maintain a compliance pack per shipment (invoice, packing list, product datasheet, HS-6 classification, end-user certificate) to avoid payment holds; (viii) Statutory reporting of outbound payments is captured by the bank at source in the filière déléguée; single transactions above €1,000,000 may trigger a request for the underlying contract to close the BOP file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX Forwards (change à terme ferme) on EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/GBP — with documented underlying commercial exposure evidenced by invoices, purchase orders, or LC values to satisfy the MiFID II 'actual or effective' hedging requirement for non-financial counterparties; tenors up to 18 months are standard for a hardware trade cycle.
FX Swaps (swap de change) for short-date treasury liquidity management — simultaneous spot and forward legs to cover temporary currency gaps without creating an open speculative position.

Cross-currency swaps (swaps de devises, XCCY) for long-term project receivables in USD or CNY matched against EUR funding — permissible for structured smart-meter export contracts with defined milestone cash flows and an interest profile.

Vanilla FX Options (call/put options on EUR against USD and CNY) — purchased-premium strategies or zero-cost collars (achat de tunnel) to cap conversion downside in export tenders while retaining upside; covered option-writing by corporates is strictly limited and requires explicit bank approval.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on EUR/CNY (offshore CNH referencing the CFETS onshore fix) — permitted where the onshore CNY market is unavailable for hedging a documented cross-border receivable; settlement in EUR against the CFETS 9:15 am Beijing fix with full documentation of the physical trade flow.

Trade-finance-package hedges — the French bank locks an FX forward together with the discounting rate of an export LC, providing a two-way price for dual-currency milestone LCs and eliminating basis risk between the LC proceeds and the EUR operating account.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts filing (Comptes Annuels, management report and auditor report when applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via Guichet Unique / Registre National des Entreprises (RNE-INPI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of fiscal year-end; for a 31 December close, no later than 31 July (Code de commerce Art. L.232-23)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered injunction with fine up to EUR 15,000 per manager; delayed filing penalties; two consecutive years of non-filing triggers administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minutes of the Ordinary Annual General Meeting approving the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book plus copy lodged with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM to be convened within 6 months of fiscal year-end; minutes lodged at RCS within 1 month of the meeting date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability of the gérant; shareholder petition to court to order the meeting; invalidity risk for dividend distributions resolved at the AGM

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner (UBO) confirmation declaration associated with the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre National des Entreprises via INPI/Guichet Unique (Anti-Money Laundering File, CMF Art. L.561-2 et seq.)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the accounts filing; for any share transfer event, re-file updated UBO declaration within 30 days of the transfer registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative registry lock and fines up to EUR 5,000 for repeated non-confirmation; convention of non-disclosure does not cure the filing gap

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporation tax declaration package (Liasse Fiscale 2065-SD, 2052, 2053, 2054 and ancillary schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — corporate income tax service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year, filed by 3 May of the following year; for other year-ends, within 3 months of the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of assessed IS plus 0.4% monthly late-payment interest; possible EUR 150 fixed fine; enforcement collection by DGFiP

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business tax payment (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises) for the operating premises and registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP local tax collection office (issued as direct debit notice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable by 15 December of the current tax year based on prior-year rental value assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late payment penalty plus 0.7% per month in delay interest; enforced recovery against the SARL's assets

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a Commissaire aux Comptes when the SARL exceeds, at the year-end, at least two of the following three thresholds: total balance sheet ≥ EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT ≥ EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees during the fiscal year ≥ 50 (Code de commerce Art. D.821-127)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) as codified by ANC Regulation 2014-03 and subsequent ANC updates; IFRS is not mandatory for standalone SARL statutory financial statements

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership must be reconfirmed annually with the RNE alongside the annual accounts filing; any transfer of shares or change of control requires an updated UBO declaration within 30 days of the transfer date; the registry record remains blocked and the SARL is exposure to AMF/administrative fines if confirmation lapses
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes and Decisions Record Book (Registre des Décisions des Associés)
Share Transfer Records (Registre des Mouvements de Titres)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $500 – $2,800 for Paris/Pau domiciliation services and legal representative address
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $6,000 – $22,000 for a certified audit of a smart-meter manufacturing SARL, dependent on inventory complexity and group reporting

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs; Research Tax Credit (CIR) 30% on eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) 20% for SMEs; reduced 10% patent box rate for net income from qualifying industrial property; Young Innovative Company (JEI) partial exemptions. Note: French tax loss carryforward is statutorily indefinite but annually capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding that threshold; the 5 in the schema field is a template indicator, not a statutory limit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 2065-SD (liasse fiscale); mandatory electronic filing via impots.gouv.fr or EDI/EFI transmission.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, supplemented by four quarterly corporate income tax instalment payments (15 Mar, 15 Jun, 15 Sep, 15 Dec).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after fiscal year close; for a 31 December year-end, the standard deadline is 3 May of the following year, with extensions available under the electronic filing calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identity, registered office, SIREN/SIRET, RCS number, share capital, business activity code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the French permanent establishment (PE) address and French tax representative identification; non-resident entities must also declare their PE registration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book profit, non-deductible charges, tax-free income, add-backs and deductions, resulting in taxable result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source income attributable to the PE under CGI Article 209; provide PE allocation statements in 2058-B.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward amount brought forward, current-year use, and remaining deficit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident may use deficits of the French PE to the extent they are attributable to the PE and otherwise deductible under domestic law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for research tax credit, innovation tax credit, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach documentation proving eligible French R&D/innovation activity; foreign tax credit claims require a tax residence certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 10% of the tax due; late-payment interest at 0.5% per month; 40% penalty for abusive or fraudulent filing; EUR 15,000 penalty for failure to produce transfer pricing documentation on request.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% dividend withholding tax on payments to non-resident corporate shareholders; 30% final withholding tax for non-resident individuals (12.8% income tax plus 17.2% social levies). The distributing French company also bears a 3% surtax on distributions under Article 235 ter ZCA CGI.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholders must provide an annual French 'attestation de résidence fiscale' (Form 5000/5001) to the payer before the dividend payment can benefit from a reduced DTA rate. If treaty-reduced withholding was not applied at source, a refund is claimed from the French tax office (SIE) on Form 2091. For EU parent-subsidiary directive relief, the direct parent must hold at least 10% of the relevant capital for at least two years, satisfy substance conditions, and file Form 1016-B for 0% withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law: royalties paid to non-residents are subject to 33.33% withholding under CGI Article 182B; interest paid to non-residents is subject to 30% withholding under CGI Article 125A, subject to exemptions for ordinary experienced credit institutions, EU-resident lenders, and treaty-creditable claims. Treaty positions: royalty withholding generally ranges from 0% to 10% depending on the DTA; interest withholding is frequently 0% under the EU Interest & Royalty Directive and many French double-tax agreements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50 million annual turnover excluding tax for the French entity, or when the SARL directly or indirectly controls, or is controlled by, a foreign enterprise; EU master/local file also required where the group has consolidated turnover of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not administer a Gulf-style ESR code, but applies equivalent anti-abuse and substance doctrines through CGI Articles 209-B and 155-A and LPF Article L64. A French SARL must demonstrate genuine economic substance – premises, employees, management decisions, local books and records – in order to preserve treaty benefits and avoid recharacterisation of its operations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting a liasse fiscale omitting French turnover from smart electricity meter/IoT device sales; using undisclosed foreign bank accounts or crypto payment rails; knowingly inflating deductible costs with artificial invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty under CGI Article 1741: up to EUR 500,000 fine (or 50% of the concealed tax amount, whichever is higher) and 5 years imprisonment. Civil/administrative re-assessment may apply an 80% penalty for abuse of law under CGI Article 1729(b), plus late-payment interest at 0.5% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant or de facto director is jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax, penalties and interest; criminal conviction triggers travel bans, disqualification, attachment of personal assets, and orders prohibiting exit from national territory.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing failure / TP documentation breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intercompany sales, licensing, or service contracts for smart metering devices priced outside arm's length; benchmark using zero-margin cost-plus without functional analysis; failure to prepare or file Master File/Local File when thresholds are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority may reassess taxable income at arm's length; 40% penalty on unjustified benefit transfer plus 0.5% monthly interest; separate EUR 15,000 fine per French entity for non-communication of TP documentation under LPF Article L13-AA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs false invoices or deliberately approves fabricated intercompany agreements is exposed to criminal fraud liability and may be separately assessed for the tax due; management fault may lead to personal contribution toward the corporate deficit in insolvency proceedings (action en comblement de passif).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / artful abuse of law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a SARL as a letter-box company with no French office, no employees, no physical meeting of managers, and no real economic activity; using nominee directors to conceal actual control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of LPF Article L64: the transaction is set aside and an 80% penalty is imposed, plus interest; VAT registration may be terminated; sales may be re-qualified into the source state leading to reverse-charge penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: French insolvency law permits piercing the veil where there is confusion of patrimonies or fictitious legal acts, resulting in personal liability and a travel ban; a nominee director faces up to EUR 5,000 fine and disqualification from acting as a manager.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the beneficial-owner declaration with the RCS; using opaque trusts or foreign shell layers to hide the ultimate natural-person shareholder of the SARL; conducting international project wire transfers without suspicious transaction controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Beneficial-owner declaration breach: EUR 5,000 fine for natural persons and EUR 25,000 for companies under Article L561-2-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code; money laundering under Article 324-1 of the Penal Code carries up to 5 years imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine, or 10 years and EUR 750,000 where aggravated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who intentionally conceals beneficial ownership, hides funds, or facilitates laundering of project payments faces criminal prosecution, asset seizure, international travel restrictions, and disqualification from managing any commercial company for up to 15 years.
